flawed_step: The universal claim (Tait's conjecture) fails: 3-connected cubic planar graphs need not be Hamiltonian.
counterexample: The Tutte graph (46 vertices, 69 edges) is cubic, planar and 3-connected, and it is not Hamiltonian. These are standard published facts, not re-checked edge by edge here. Construction: take a central vertex v and three copies of the 15-vertex Tutte fragment. Each copy has three outgoing edges a, b, c. Join v to each copy's a-edge and join the b/c edges of the copies in a ring around the outside. Argument: each fragment is attached by exactly 3 edges, so a Hamiltonian cycle uses exactly 2 of them. Tutte's case analysis of the fragment (cited, not re-derived here) shows those 2 edges must include edge a. So the cycle would use all 3 edges at v, which is impossible.
assessment_summary: The statement is Tait's conjecture, which Tutte disproved in 1946. The Tutte graph meets every hypothesis and has no Hamiltonian cycle. The top-level argument (3 attaching edges per fragment, so each fragment's a-edge is forced and v would get degree 3 in the cycle) was checked. The fragment's key property and the graph's 3-connectivity are cited from the standard result, not re-verified here.
